affectedCopies: Compliance obligation surfaces (/compliance/obligations and the regulation detail page)

privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: not-applicable — the row states a regulator's rule (a duration and the categories it binds) and attaches it to a regulation. It describes no person.
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: No data-subject workflow is introduced or changed. Retention windows are unaffected in both directions: the row's stated minimum does not change, only which regulation it hangs from, and foldObligationFloors reads the minimum rather than the citation.

migration.name: none — seed convergence, no schema change
migration.backfill: The seed now looks a floor's obligation up by `reference` alone rather than by (regulationId, reference), so a floor that has moved to the regulation it names re-points the EXISTING row instead of minting a second one. On an install that already seeded the misattributed public-sector floor, the next seed run moves that row from REG-US-EPA-NPDES to REG-US-STATE-PUBLIC-RECORDS. On a fresh install nothing moves. On this development install no retention-floor obligation has been seeded yet, so the first run is pure create.
migration.rollback: Forward-only and fully reversible by the same mechanism: reverting the code makes the next seed re-point the row back by the old alphabetical pick. Nothing is deleted, so nothing is unrecoverable.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Obligation is a regulated compliance record and stays one. No row is created, destroyed, or re-identified by this change: an existing seeded floor keeps its id, its obligationId, its linked controls and its collected evidence, and only its parent regulation changes. Delete-and-recreate was considered and rejected precisely because it would orphan those links.

fields.reason: A floor moves from the regulation that merely sorted first alphabetically to the regulation it names. Without the move the platform cites the Clean Water Act as the source of a records-retention minimum on chat transcripts, which is a compliance claim it must not make (BI-0C723E18). The move is an update in place, so the obligation's identity and its relationships survive it.
fields.provenance: BI-0C723E18; verified against this install's 63 active regulations: 5 of 5 floors attach by preference after the fix, 4 of 5 before it.

fields.reason: The lookup is now keyed on `reference` alone, which is this seed's own idempotency key and is written by no other code path. A hand-authored obligation cannot match, so operator-authored compliance content is out of range. At most one row per reference can exist, because before this change a floor could attach to only one regulation.
